explicit_propositions.text: True worship involves both an inner reality and an outer expression.
Worship is not limited to Sunday services or internal feelings; it extends into daily life.
A true worshiper consistently focuses on the Lord throughout all areas of life—workplace, home, hobbies, sports.
Outward expressions of worship include loving and serving others, which reflects the light of Jesus.
When believers live out worship, others may be led to God, fulfilling a divine purpose.
Drifting from God typically begins subtly—just one degree off course—and accumulates over time.
Even a small deviation from God’s direction can result in significant spiritual distance over time.
The metaphor of navigation illustrates how minor distractions can lead to major spiritual misalignment.
Repentance allows individuals to realign their lives toward God, even after prolonged drift.
Focusing on God one degree more leads to transformation in personal relationships, finances, and worldview.

assumptions.text: Spiritual alignment with God is measurable and incremental, not binary.
Believers possess agency to intentionally choose greater devotion to God in any moment.
God values consistent, embodied worship over ritualistic or isolated acts.
The human heart naturally tends toward distraction and idolatry without continual recalibration.
Scripture provides trustworthy guidance for understanding true worship and moral direction.
External actions reflect internal spiritual condition, and vice versa.
Others’ lives are positively impacted when individuals pursue deeper intimacy with God.
Small, repeated choices compound into lasting spiritual outcomes.
The Christian life is meant to be lived continuously, not confined to moments of religious observance.
Divine forgiveness enables ongoing restoration and renewed commitment despite past failure.
